---
title: "Pairwise errors from joint posterior draws"
subtitle: "4.11 · after postrank’s posterior-input vignettes"
description: "Dependence of empirical pairwise errors on the alignment of unit values within posterior states."
---

A posterior draw contains one joint state of every unit on every criterion. The empirical error probability of a
proposed direction is the proportion of states in which that direction is wrong. The package's 32-state toy sample
illustrates the role of alignment: cyclically shifting one unit's vector preserves its marginal values but changes
its pairing with the other units. Shifting all units together instead permutes complete states and preserves
full-sample pairwise errors. The display records both counts and denominators, including the effects of using only a
prefix of the retained sample.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Original states.** Among the 32 retained states, placing 001 above site-B is wrong 8 times on need_A and
  32 times on need_B. The empirical error shares are .250 and 1. Each complete state specifies the order of all three units on both criteria.
- **Shift one unit.** Moving site-B’s whole two-criterion vector forward cyclically changes the need_A count to
  7 times and its share to .219. The need_B count remains 32 times. The raw marginal values have only been
  reordered; the joint pairing has changed.
- **Move states together.** Applying the same shift to every unit restores the original full-sample counts:
  8 times and 32 times. This is a reordering of complete states, so every full-sample coefficient stays the same.
- **Short prefix.** Only 8 retained states now enter the estimates. Both the wrong count and denominator depend on the selected prefix length. Short prefixes can change even when complete states
  are shifted together.
- **Unshifted pair.** The pair 001 and site C contains neither shifted unit. Its counts remain 0 times and
  25 times, with need_B share .781. Changing a third unit’s pairing cannot change this pair’s comparisons.
- **Full cycle.** A full cyclic shift returns every source vector to its original row, with counts 8 times and
  32 times again. The source table retains all original unit and criterion coordinates.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
This is a fixed IID numerical sample from a specified synthetic normal law. A zero empirical error share means
that the event did not occur in this sample; it does not establish an exact zero posterior probability. The shift
is a reproducible dependence illustration, not an additional posterior simulation or a convergence test.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
e <- postrank_pairwise(postrank_toy)$e
e["001", "site-B", ]  # need_A .25, need_B 1
```
:::
